terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: prestressed concrete lighting pole with a clamped steel bracket arm and a cobra-head lantern
motionPotential: none - a direct-buried concrete pole, rigid body
objectClass.notes: The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.454 against the declared 0.213, so it carries the fixture and not the assembly proportions. This is the cheap provincial variant: the lantern is CLAMPED to an ordinary concrete pole rather than carried on a purpose-made column.

reasoning: Four macro/meso parts: the concrete pole, the clamped steel bracket arm, the cast lantern and its refractor.
No repetition systems: a direct-buried pole has no baseplate and no bolts, which is the visible difference from the steel column variant.
The pole is a SQUARE section, not octagonal - a tapered-sweep with radialSegments 4 and a 45 degree twist gives an axis-aligned rectangle whose half-extents are 0.707 of the authored radius.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. Four drawn parts and the sub-structure - taper, bracket clamp, arm rise, lantern wedge, bowl seating - carried as localFeatures because each component costs a draw call.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A tapered square section 0.215 m at the foot and 0.135 m at the top.
A short chamfered cap closing the pole's top on all four faces.
Thirteen recessed lifting and fixing holes down one face between 1.10 and 6.60 m.
Green algae over the bottom 3 m, as an axis tint multiplied into the concrete.
Pale patches where the cast surface has broken away to the aggregate, as a canvas tile.
Two steel bands wrapping the pole, the only fixing the bracket has.
A strut from the lower band to mid-arm, without which the arm floats.
A cast wedge tapering from spigot to nose over a refractor bowl.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The pole section is square: the plate shows two flat faces meeting at a vertical arris with different shading. Confidence 0.85.
The far side of the pole and lantern is not in the single view; mirrored about the arm plane. Confidence 0.85.
Pole width is engineering-derived (0.315 m across flats at the base for an 8 m pole, matching the declared 0.30 m depth envelope), NOT scaled from the plate, which would give 1.26 m. Confidence 0.85.

The plate shows a row of small circular lifting/cable holes down the pole face. They are not built: at 8 m they are a few pixels and each would need geometry the budget cannot carry. Recorded as an omission. Confidence 0.9.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: pole reads square and tapered, not round
per-material rendered luma against the measured 148/119/158/201
turntable hole gate at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees
the algae band fades out by ~3 m rather than tinting the whole pole
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not take proportion from the plate or the Meshy proxy; both carry the plate's square framing.
Do not give this pole a baseplate or holding-down bolts - it is direct-buried, and that is the visible difference from the steel-column variant.
Do not author a fifth material for the algae; it is a colour region on the concrete.
Do not add a pivot per component or any socket.
Do not seat the refractor flush with the housing underside, or butt the bracket cap against the pole face - coincident co-facing surfaces z-fight.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FOUR components across four material layers: the pole and its bracket arm as macro, the luminaire and refractor as meso. Eight micro-feature groups sit inside them -- square taper, chamfered cap, thirteen cast holes, the algae band, two clamp bands, the diagonal strut, the cobra wedge and the refractor bowl.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 1.70 x 8.00 x 0.30 m within the asset's 10% tolerance, with outreach/height reading ~0.21 rather than the plate's 0.45.

featureReviewTargets.name: Square tapered concrete pole
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The pole must be a TAPERED SQUARE section with a chamfered cap and a column of recessed cast holes down one face. A smooth round cylinder fails -- that is what the previous build shipped, and the asset notes call the holes identity-defining.

featureReviewTargets.name: Clamped bracket arm
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The bracket must read as BANDS wrapping the pole with a diagonal strut under the arm, not as an arm growing out of the shaft.

featureReviewTargets.name: Cobra-head wedge profile
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Shallow at the spigot, swelling to full width, closing to a blunt nose, flat underside, refractor below.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Concrete, steel, aluminium and acrylic must separate by value against the measured 148 / 119 / 158 / 201, and NO surface may render near the ~58 backdrop at any azimuth.

featureReviewTargets.name: Algae staining at the foot
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Green algae must be concentrated over the bottom third and gone by about 3 m, carried as a tint on the concrete rather than as a separate material.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: concrete 148 / bracket steel 119 / aluminium 158 / acrylic 201 in measured plate luma; the render must keep the ordering.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as four named parts. Not articulated and not breakable: destructionGroups is empty on the asset and no component carries a fractureGroup.

assumptions: The pole section is square: the plate shows two flat faces meeting at a vertical arris with different shading. Confidence 0.85.
The far side of the pole and the lantern is mirrored across the arm plane; the single view cannot show it. Confidence 0.85.
Pole width is engineering-derived at 0.315 m across flats, matching the declared 0.30 m depth envelope. Scaling the plate by its arm span would give a 1.26 m pole.

The row of small circular lifting and cable holes down the pole face is NOT built. At 8 m they are a few pixels each and would need geometry the budget cannot carry; recorded as a deliberate omission.
No cabling, conduit or clamp bolts are modelled - thin geometry the budget cannot carry.
Metalness is authored below a physical 1.0 on both metals because the review harness carries no environment map.
The lantern's internal gear tray is not modelled: the kit builds exterior shells only.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the pole's square section on the ground plane (y=0). This pole is direct-buried, so there is no baseplate between it and the ground.

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 1.688 x 8.000 x 0.290 m against the declared 1.7 x 8 x 0.3 -- within 1% on width and height and 3% on depth. Width is the 1.5 m bracket reach plus the shaft, exactly as the asset notes describe it; depth is set by the luminaire, which is the only thing on the prop wider than the 0.215 m pole.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about the XY plane (z=0), the plane containing the pole axis and the outreach direction
silhouette.notes: The plate is square-framed at aspect 0.454 against the declared 0.213 and photographs a shorter pole, so it is authoritative for the fixture and not for the assembly proportions.

componentTree.name: Tapered square prestressed pole with cast holes and algae
componentTree.topologyRationale: A tapered SQUARE frustum, not a cylinder. The whole shaft is 12 triangles because `frusta` takes a footprint at each end, which is what leaves room for the cast holes and the bracket gear to be real geometry. The previous build was a smooth round pipe with none of it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. One frustum 0.215 m square at the foot tapering to 0.135 m at 7.94 m, closed by a short chamfered cap; thirteen recessed cast holes down the +Z face between 1.10 m and 6.60 m; green algae as an axis tint over the bottom 3 m.

localFeatures.description: 0.215 m square at the base tapering to 0.135 m -- the asset notes give about 0.2 m square at the base. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION, not the plate: silh.mjs puts the plate's subject at 396 x 904 px, which at the declared 8 m height would imply a 3.50 m width against the declared 1.7.
A short frustum pulling in on all four faces at the top, which is how a cast pole is finished and what stops the shaft reading as a cut-off box.

Thirteen recessed holes at even spacing down one face between 1.10 and 6.60 m. These are the lifting and fixing holes of a real spun-and-cast Thai pole and the asset notes call them identity-defining. Built as recesses rather than through-holes: at any distance a player sees an 8 m pole from they read identically, and a boolean would cost far more than the shading does.
Green algae over the bottom 3 m as an axis tint MULTIPLIED into the concrete rather than a second material. The plate's staining is strongest at the foot and gone by about 3 m.

componentTree.notes: Concrete #9d9c94 with a darker cap #8e8d86 and hole recesses #4e4d48 as vertex colours, plus a spalled-patch tile.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Cast concrete carrying its chamfered cap, its hole recesses and its algae band as vertex colours, with spalled patches as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Band clamp and diagonal strut carrying the lantern
componentTree.topologyRationale: Painted steel is a different substance from the concrete it clamps to, and the clamp is the whole reason this prop is a lamp bolted to an ordinary distribution pole rather than a purpose-made column.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two bands wrapping the pole at 6.87 m and 7.21 m, a 1.40 m horizontal arm off the upper one, and a diagonal strut rotated 0.60 rad from the lower band up to mid-arm.

localFeatures.description: Two steel bands wrapping the pole 22 mm proud of its faces, which is how the plate's bracket is fixed -- there is no cast boss and no bolt flange.
A strut from the lower band up to mid-arm. Without it the arm reads as floating off the pole, and the plate shows it clearly.

componentTree.notes: Steel #8b8378 at metalness 0.30 -- the plate's bracket is rusted and matt, not galvanised.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Rusted painted steel, matt and warm against the cool concrete.

componentTree.name: Cast cobra-head luminaire
componentTree.topologyRationale: Cast aluminium against the rusted bracket steel and the concrete: three substances, three material layers, which is what the quality contract requires.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Three stacked boxes spanning 0.70 m along the arm, deepest at the spigot and tapering to the nose, the widest 0.29 m deep.

localFeatures.description: A wedge tapering from spigot to nose. Its 0.29 m depth is what sets the declared 0.30 m envelope depth -- at 0.23 the measured bbox came in 23% under the declaration.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A smooth light casting, the coolest and brightest metal on the prop.

componentTree.name: Acrylic refractor bowl
componentTree.topologyRationale: The only non-metal on the prop and the second meso component.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 12-segment cylinder scaled 1.30 along the arm, hung below the housing.

localFeatures.description: Hung proud of the casting rather than flush with its underside: co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A pale prismatic bowl, the brightest surface on the prop.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 1.688 x 8.000 x 0.290 m against the declared 1.7 x 8 x 0.3 -- within 1% on width and height and 3% on depth. Width is the 1.5 m bracket reach plus the shaft, exactly as the asset notes describe it. Proportion comes from the DECLARATION: silh.mjs puts the plate's subject at 396 x 904 px, which at 8 m tall would imply a 3.50 m width.

A tapered SQUARE frustum, 0.215 m at the foot to 0.135 m at the top, with a chamfered cap and thirteen recessed cast holes down one face between 1.10 and 6.60 m. The previous build was a smooth round cylinder with none of it, against asset notes that call the holes identity-defining. The whole shaft is 12 triangles as one frustum, which is what left room for the holes and the bracket gear to be real geometry.

Two steel BANDS wrapping the pole 22 mm proud of its faces, a 1.40 m arm off the upper one, and a diagonal strut from the lower band up to mid-arm. The strut matters: without it the arm reads as floating off the pole, and the plate shows it clearly. There is no cast boss and no bolt flange on the real thing -- the clamp is the whole reason this is a lamp bolted to an ordinary distribution pole rather than a purpose-made column.

A three-box cast wedge tapering from a 0.29 m spigot to a 0.22 m nose over an acrylic refractor bowl hung proud of the casting. Its depth is what sets the declared 0.30 m envelope depth -- at 0.23 the measured bbox came in 23% under. Not carried: the plate's lantern is tilted nose-down and mine is level, which is a real difference and is why this is 0.90 rather than higher.

Four material layers: weathered concrete #9d9c94 measured off the plate's subject mask (p25 106,106,98 / p50 127,126,121 / p75 167,164,149), rusted bracket steel #8b8378 at metalness 0.30 -- painted and rusting rather than hot-dipped, unlike the galvanised columns elsewhere in this kit -- cast aluminium #a8adad and acrylic #d6dad4. Luma 126 is clear of the 55.5-60.5 band gatecrop's alpha key erases, so no lift was needed.

Green algae over the bottom 3 m as an axis tint MULTIPLIED into the concrete rather than a second material, which is what the plate shows -- strongest at the foot and gone by about 3 m. Pale spalled patches where the surface has broken to the aggregate ride on the same material as a post-construction canvas tile. What is NOT carried is the plate's rust bleed running down from the clamp, which is directional and the tile is isotropic.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to hero2x with the lighting kit and DELIBERATELY UNDERSPENT: the build measures 468 triangles at 4 draw calls, 4 materials and 4 geometries. A tapered square pole is 12 triangles as one frustum, which is exactly why the cast holes, the band clamp and the diagonal strut can all be real geometry and still leave the prop at 3% of its triangle ceiling.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left: the pole's left face reads brighter than its right and the lantern crown is the brightest surface.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides are lifted rather than black, at roughly a 0.7 shadow-to-key ratio.
No separate rim is visible in the plate - the object separates from the backdrop by value alone.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A near-white seamless backdrop at luma ~245 fills the frame; foreground coverage is 11.2%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot. A direct-buried concrete pole has no moving parts; one root pivot at base-center is the complete correct answer, not a gap.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. Nothing clips onto this prop: the lantern is carried on its own bracket and the bracket is clamped to the pole.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
